extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers (referees) for Nature Portfolio journals, including Nature Communications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio journals (e.g., Nature Communications). Covers what is peer-reviewed, editorial triage, reviewer selection, confidentiality, what to address in referee reports, and procedural policies (anonymity, AI use, timing, transparent review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of contributions that are peer-reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: The following types of contribution to Nature Portfolio journals are peer-reviewed: Articles, Letters, Brief Communications, Matters Arising, Technical Reports, Analysis, Resources, Reviews, Perspectives and Insight articles. Correspondence and published corrections may also be peer-reviewed at editors' discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other contributed articles are not usually peer-reviewed, but editors may choose to peer-review articles in these sections if they present technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publication (overall editorial standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper should represent an advance in understanding likely to influence thinking in the field, with strong evidence for its conclusions, and there should be a discernible reason why the work deserves the visibility of publication in a Nature Portfolio journal rather than the best specialist journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should weigh novelty, conceptual advance, and strength of evidence when assessing suitability for the journal's readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial triage (initial screening)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted manuscripts are read by editorial staff; only those that seem most likely to meet editorial criteria are sent for formal review. Manuscripts judged insufficient in general interest or otherwise inappropriate are rejected promptly without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prompt rejections may be based on informal specialist advice. Reviewers should be aware that not all manuscripts reach external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers and decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts sent for formal review are typically sent to two or three reviewers, sometimes more for specialist advice. Editors make decisions based on reviewers' advice but not by counting votes; they evaluate the strength of arguments and may consider other information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible editorial decisions include accept (with/without editorial revisions), invite revision to address specific concerns, reject but indicate further work might justify resubmission, or reject outright for lack of novelty, insufficient conceptual advance, or major technical/interpretational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer commitment to reassess revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers agree to assess a paper, this is considered a commitment to review subsequent revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will not necessarily return a resubmitted paper to reviewers if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms. Reviewers should be willing to provide follow-up advice as requested, though editors try to minimize prolonged disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting peer-reviewers (selection criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are selected based on many factors, including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and editors' previous experience of a reviewer's characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors favour referees who are quick, careful, and provide reasoning for their views (whether robustly critical or forgiving). Springer Nature is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion and encourages diverse demographic representation among reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of peer review materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, authors and reviewers must keep confidential all details of the editorial and peer review process on submitted manuscripts. Reviewers must maintain confidentiality of manuscripts and related materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer seeks advice from colleagues, they must consult the editor first and provide the names of any colleagues used. Confidential material (correspondence, reports) must not be published or disclosed without prior written consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the literature for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer lacks access to a published paper necessary for evaluation, the journal will obtain and supply a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should send the publication reference required to the handling editor, who will obtain the paper and pay any necessary fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of a review (what reports should achieve)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose is to provide editors with the information needed to reach a decision and to instruct authors on how to strengthen their paper to make it acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative reviews should explain major weaknesses so that rejected authors can understand the basis for the decision and what needs to be done to improve the manuscript for other journals. Confidential comments to the editor are welcome but should not contradict the main points to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (what to summarise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please summarise what you consider to be the outstanding features of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise statement of the main findings and their importance to help editors quickly grasp the paper's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity (identify fatal flaws)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript have flaws which should prohibit its publication? If so, please provide details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify technical, methodological, or interpretational problems that undermine the paper's validity and state why they are prohibitive for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conclusions are not original, provide relevant references; do you feel the results are of immediate interest to many in your discipline and/or to people from several disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both novelty and broader significance across disciplines; cite prior work showing lack of originality when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & methodology (completeness and reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the validity of the approach, quality of the data and quality of presentation. Reviewers are expected to review all data, including extended data and supplementary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporting of data and methodology is sufficiently detailed and transparent to enable reproduction of results; point out missing details and recommend how to improve data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of statistics and treatment of uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: All error bars should be defined in figure legends; include a specific comment on the appropriateness of statistical tests and the accuracy of descriptions of error bars and probability values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly check statistical methods, definitions of error bars, p-values, confidence intervals and treatment of uncertainties; flag misuse or misreporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions (robustness and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you find that the conclusions and data interpretation are robust, valid and reliable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether conclusions follow from the data and analyses, whether alternative interpretations exist, and whether claims are overstated relative to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements (recommended additional work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please list additional experiments or data that could help strengthen the work in a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what additional analyses, controls, or experiments would address weaknesses and whether they are feasible within a reasonable revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: References (appropriateness of literature cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this manuscript reference previous literature appropriately? If not, what references should be included or excluded?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing critical citations and any inappropriate or excessive citation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context (abstract, introduction, conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the abstract clear and accessible? Are abstract, introduction and conclusions appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, structure, and whether the manuscript places results in proper conceptual context for intended readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflammatory or potentially libelous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript contain any language that is inappropriate or potentially libelous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag any wording that could be legally problematic or unnecessarily inflammatory and recommend revisions to tone or wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity & inclusion concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion; reviewers should raise any concerns that may impact this commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note issues such as demographic representation in study samples, biased framing, or other matters that could affect DEI principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of expertise (declare limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate any particular part of the manuscript, data, or analyses that you feel is outside the scope of your expertise, or that you were unable to assess fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being explicit about limits helps editors interpret the weight of the review and decide if additional specialist opinion is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report style and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should document the referees' thought process; all statements should be justified and argued in detail, naming facts and citing supporting references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all aspects apply to every paper; when in doubt about discipline-specific standards, reviewers can contact the editor for guidance. Reports do not need to follow the suggested order but should be thorough and evidence-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: While Springer Nature explores safe AI tools, peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools. If any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, reviewers must declare such use transparently in their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers remain accountable for accuracy and should be cautious about AI limitations (outdated knowledge, biased or false outputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing (promptness and communication of delays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to respond promptly within the number of days agreed, and if they anticipate a longer delay they should inform the editor so alternatives can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt, reliable turnaround is valued; notifying editors of delays helps manage the editorial timeline and author expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and signing reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees' identities are not released to authors or other reviewers unless the referee voluntarily signs their comments. Reviewers may sign reports but should consider that reports are shared with other reviewers and that signing may complicate later interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not identify themselves to authors while the manuscript is under consideration without the editor's knowledge. The journal will not confirm or deny speculation about reviewer identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Nature-branded and Communications journals offer double-anonymized peer review where authors remain anonymous to referees; authors choosing this option are responsible for anonymizing their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A checklist is provided to help authors anonymize; reviewers should consult the specific journal website for availability and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review (publication of review materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Nature journals publish details about the peer review process (reviewer comments, author rebuttals, editorial decision letters) as part of the publication; in many journals authors can opt in at completion of peer review, while some Communications journals apply transparent review to all published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript was transferred from another Nature Portfolio journal, reviewer reports or rebuttals from the originating journal will not be published. Peer review files are supplementary and do not contain confidential editorial discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing referees' reports (offensive or confidential content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy is not to suppress reviewers' reports; comments intended for authors are transmitted. On rare occasions, editors may edit a report to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should avoid needless offence but are encouraged to state their opinions plainly. Confidential comments to editors should not contradict main points to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review publication policies (reviewer suggestions, exclusions, and transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions selected for peer review are sent to at least one, usually two or more independent reviewers. Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and request exclusion of one or two individuals or laboratories; editors usually honour such requests but the editor's decision is final. Referee comments are transferred with manuscript transfers within Nature Portfolio; identities may also be transferred for in-house editor transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors reserve the right to contact funders, regulatory bodies, journals and authors’ institutions in cases of suspected misconduct. Reviewers should be aware of how transfers affect confidentiality and report handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and security concerns in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may seek advice on aspects of a paper that raise ethical issues, data or materials access, or societal/security implications; such concerns may be considered alongside technical review and the editor makes the ultimate publication decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review raises ethical or security flags (e.g., potential misuse, dual-use issues, data access restrictions), reviewers should flag these and the editor may solicit simultaneous specialized advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and goals of peer review (selection and quality assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is designed to select technically valid research of significant interest; referees are expected to identify flaws, suggest improvements and assess novelty. Referees ensure internal consistency and help ferret out spurious conclusions or clumsy frauds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize tension between strictness and enabling novel challenges to prevailing paradigms; editors balance these to serve readers and the scientific community.
